name: Samarium
occurrence: Found alongside other lanthanides in monazite and samarskite ores (the latter lending it its name).
majorUses: Samarium-cobalt permanent magnets (heat-resistant, used in aerospace/military)
notableCharacteristics: Was the first element named after a person (Vasili Samarsky-Bykhovets, a Russian mine official), via the mineral samarskite.
ncertRelevance: first element indirectly named after a real person
whyHere: Its six unpaired 4f electrons give strong magnetic behaviour that, when alloyed with cobalt, retains its magnetism at much higher temperatures than neodymium magnets — exactly why it's chosen for aerospace and military uses despite being pricier.
didYouKnow: Samarium was the first element ever named, even indirectly, after a real living person — via the mineral samarskite, named for the mining engineer who supplied the sample it was isolated from.
genZNote: First element with a person's name attached, even indirectly. Started the whole 'name it after someone' trend.
